conviction_note: Near non-result: no consensus bar, no guidance, and the Q3 report is the first full quarter of a newly merged fintech plus a Venezuelan oil stake, so the size is large (8%) and the sign barely leans (p_up 45). The lean comes from the cash spent on PetroUrdaneta ($27.5m, $22.15m of it paid on 17 Nov), the stated need to find development financing, and two of the last four report days falling 8.7% and 12.7%. It is held near 50 because the stock is already down 37% in 20 sessions and the register shows no disclosed short. The findings sum to -0.9 and the scaled number is -0.8. They roughly agree because neither measurement has much in it.

findings.finding: The Q3 release will show cash after the PetroUrdaneta payments ($5.35m at signing in Q3, $22.15m closing on 17 Nov from existing cash). The company says it is 'focus[ing] on securing financing to further develop the asset', and KEO Energy has a credit-facility framework of up to $350m to PetroUrdaneta. Together these raise the odds that the report or the call signals new financing or dilution.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last two transformational releases sold: Q2 report (31 Aug, after close) -12.7% on 1 Sep, with the Lionheart non-extension released the same evening. Q3 2025 report -8.7%. No clean prior read of a financing announcement on report day.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the payment amounts are public and the stock is down 37% in 20 sessions. What is not public is the 30 Sep cash figure, whether the company names a raise, and its size. If the market had fully priced a raise, the stock would not have bounced +2.4%/+4.1% on the 18-19 Nov closing news. Financing as a question: the money buys 16% more of a field the company now operates under an August administration agreement with PDVSA, but no reserve report or production figure has been published to say what the development returns. So the sign is negative only on dilution timing, and small.

findings.finding: The founder and former chairman Paolo Fidanza pledged 125,535,330 KEOC shares, about 36% of the 352,657,866 outstanding (FI insider register, transaction 2026-05-14, filed 2026-05-29). He left the board 'for personal reasons' on 12 Sep, and the stock fell 21% on 14 Sep. A pledged block of that size on a stock down about 60% since June is a forced-selling overhang that no longer has to be reported through the insider register.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The board exit was announced 12 Sep at 00:58 and the stock fell -21.0% on 14 Sep on 6.5m shares. No other observed instance.
findings.original_quote: 2026-05-29 | Maha Capital AB | Paolo Fidanza | Styrelseledamot | Ja | Pantsättning | Maha Capital (MAHA A) | Aktie | SE0008374383 | 2026-05-14 | 125 535 330 | Antal  (translation: board member Paolo Fidanza, closely associated party: yes, pledge of 125,535,330 shares)
findings.why_not_priced: The pledge is filed only in FI's Swedish insider register, and neither the English wire nor the company's releases mention it. Whether the pledge has been called is unknown, and the November slide (8.7 to 5.1 SEK on no company news) could be that or anything else. An unexplained drawdown is worth 0, so this is sized as an overhang that can hit on report day, not as an explanation. It is not tied to the print and it agrees with the run-down, so it is small.

findings.finding: Q2's TUSD (48,085) net loss was almost all one-off: TUSD (18,337) initial stock-based comp, TUSD (25,739) share-settled expenses and TUSD (2,323) non-recurring SG&A. Q3 should therefore print a much smaller headline loss on the same operating base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 printed a Yahoo-recorded 'beat' against an estimate and fell 12.7% the next session.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the one-offs were labelled in the Q2 release, so a narrower loss is mechanical and expected. It is filed because headline EPS will swing, and a quarter whose underlying opex of about TUSD 4.7m runs well ahead of net operating income of about TUSD 1.6m will not look better on the lines that matter.
